C. Condenses supporting arguments into a unified takeaway
D. Announces the controlling idea of a single body paragraph
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Hook) → B (Captures reader curiosity on the very first line); 2 (Thesis statement) → A (Declares the essay's central claim and analytical scope); 3 (Topic sentence) → D (Announces the controlling idea of a single body paragraph); 4 (Concluding synthesis) → C (Condenses supporting arguments into a unified takeaway). Insho tuzilmasi qismlari: Hook (qiziqtirish), Thesis (asosiy da'vo), Topic sentence (xatboshi g'oyasi), Concluding synthesis (xulosa).
mnemonic: Hook / Thesis statement / Topic sentence / Concluding synthesis

q:
Match each lexical cohesion mechanism with its clear example:
1. Direct repetition
2. Synonymy
3. Hyponymy
4. Collocation chain A. Connecting "orchard trees" to "figs, almonds, and pears"
B. Linking "glaciers" smoothly with "shrinking ice masses"
C. Reusing a key technical term intentionally for clarity
D. Weaving "arbiter, bishop, clock, checkmate" across lines
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Direct repetition) → C (Reusing a key technical term intentionally for clarity); 2 (Synonymy) → B (Linking "glaciers" smoothly with "shrinking ice masses"); 3 (Hyponymy) → A (Connecting "orchard trees" to "figs, almonds, and pears"); 4 (Collocation chain) → D (Weaving "arbiter, bishop, clock, checkmate" across lines). Leksik yaxlitlik: takror, sinonimiya, giponimiya (umumiy→xususiy) va kollokatsiya/mavzu maydoni.
mnemonic: Direct repetition / Synonymy / Hyponymy / Collocation chain

q:
Match each contrast connector with its precise structural nuance:
1. Whereas
2. Conversely
3. Instead
4. Nonetheless A. Reverses a claim to highlight an opposite case next
B. Replaces a rejected plan with an alternative action
C. Affirms a surprising result occurring despite an obstacle
D. Joins two contrasting clauses inside a single sentence
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Whereas) → D (Joins two contrasting clauses inside a single sentence); 2 (Conversely) → A (Reverses a claim to highlight an opposite case next); 3 (Instead) → B (Replaces a rejected plan with an alternative action); 4 (Nonetheless) → C (Affirms a surprising result occurring despite an obstacle). Kontrast bog'lovchilari nozik farqi: Whereas (bir gapda zidlik), Conversely (teskari holat), Instead (o'rniga), Nonetheless (to'siqqa qaramay).

q:
Match each cohesion flaw with how it disrupts smooth reading:
1. Ambiguous pronoun
2. Off-topic sentence
3. Missing transition
4. Broken parallelism A. Creates an abrupt logical jump between adjacent ideas
B. Leaves readers guessing which of two nouns "he/it" means
C. Inserts an unrelated fact breaking paragraph unity
D. Mixes mismatched verb forms inside a single list
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Ambiguous pronoun) → B (Leaves readers guessing which of two nouns "he/it" means); 2 (Off-topic sentence) → C (Inserts an unrelated fact breaking paragraph unity); 3 (Missing transition) → A (Creates an abrupt logical jump between adjacent ideas); 4 (Broken parallelism) → D (Mixes mismatched verb forms inside a single list). Yaxlitlik nuqsonlari: noaniq olmosh, mavzudan tashqari gap, o'tish bog'lovchisi yo'qligi va buzilgan parallelizm.
mnemonic: Ambiguous pronoun / Off-topic sentence / Missing transition / Broken parallelism

q:
Match each academic transition signal with the reader expectation it sets:
1. Namely
2. In other words
3. Above all
4. Subsequently A. Expect the next chronological step occurring afterward
B. Expect exact named items specifying a prior count
C. Expect the single most decisive priority to follow next
D. Expect a simpler rewording of a complex technical point
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Namely) → B (Expect exact named items specifying a prior count); 2 (In other words) → D (Expect a simpler rewording of a complex technical point); 3 (Above all) → C (Expect the single most decisive priority to follow next); 4 (Subsequently) → A (Expect the next chronological step occurring afterward). Akademik o'tish belgilari: Namely (aniq nomlar), In other words (qayta izoh), Above all (eng muhimi), Subsequently (keyingi bosqich).
mnemonic: Namely / In other words / Above all / Subsequently

q:
Match each reference pair with the grammatical distinction it encodes:
1. This vs. These
2. Former vs. Latter
3. Here vs. There
4. One vs. Ones A. Singular versus plural nominal substitution cleanly
B. Singular versus plural demonstrative reference
C. First-mentioned versus second-mentioned item in a pair
D. Proximal versus distal spatial reference across text
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (This vs. These) → B (Singular versus plural demonstrative reference); 2 (Former vs. Latter) → C (First-mentioned versus second-mentioned item in a pair); 3 (Here vs. There) → D (Proximal versus distal spatial reference across text); 4 (One vs. Ones) → A (Singular versus plural nominal substitution cleanly). Havola juftliklari: This/These (birlik/ko'plik), Former/Latter (1-/2-element), Here/There (yaqin/uzoq), One/Ones (ot o'rinbosari).
mnemonic: This vs. These / Former vs. Latter / Here vs. There / One vs. Ones

q:
Match each rhetorical paragraph pattern with its organizing logic:
1. Cause-and-effect
2. Problem-solution
3. Comparison-contrast
4. Chronological order A. Traces triggers leading to measurable outcomes
B. Diagnoses an obstacle and evaluates practical remedies
C. Arranges events strictly along a step-by-step timeline
D. Weighs similarities and differences between two options
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Cause-and-effect) → A (Traces triggers leading to measurable outcomes); 2 (Problem-solution) → B (Diagnoses an obstacle and evaluates practical remedies); 3 (Comparison-contrast) → D (Weighs similarities and differences between two options); 4 (Chronological order) → C (Arranges events strictly along a step-by-step timeline). Xatboshi turlari: sabab-oqibat, muammo-yechim, qiyos-kontrast va xronologik tartib.

q:
Match each shell-noun phrase with what it encapsulates from prior text:
1. This dilemma
2. These gains
3. Such oversight
4. That milestone A. Highlights a decisive breakthrough event just described
B. Collects multiple previously listed positive outcomes
C. Summarizes a tense choice between two competing goals
D. Labels an earlier mistake or neglected safeguard
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (This dilemma) → C (Summarizes a tense choice between two competing goals); 2 (These gains) → B (Collects multiple previously listed positive outcomes); 3 (Such oversight) → D (Labels an earlier mistake or neglected safeguard); 4 (That milestone) → A (Highlights a decisive breakthrough event just described). Umumlashtiruvchi otlar (shell nouns): This dilemma, These gains, Such oversight, That milestone.
mnemonic: This dilemma / These gains / Such oversight / That milestone

q:
Match each punctuation mark with its cohesive linking function:
1. Semicolon (;)
2. Colon (:)
3. Em dash (—)
4. Comma + FANBOYS A. Introduces an explanation, list, or formal quotation
B. Sets off an emphatic explanatory aside mid-sentence
C. Links two balanced main clauses via a coordinating word
D. Joins two closely related independent clauses smoothly
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Semicolon (;)) → D (Joins two closely related independent clauses smoothly); 2 (Colon (:)) → A (Introduces an explanation, list, or formal quotation); 3 (Em dash (—)) → B (Sets off an emphatic explanatory aside mid-sentence); 4 (Comma + FANBOYS) → C (Links two balanced main clauses via a coordinating word). Tinish belgilari yaxlitlikda: nuqtali vergul (yaqin mustaqil gaplar), ikki nuqta (izoh/ro'yxat), tire (urg'uli izoh), vergul+bog'lovchi.
mnemonic: Semicolon (;) / Colon (:) / Em dash (—) / Comma + FANBOYS

q:
Match each concession marker with its exact grammatical frame:
1. Although + clause
2. Despite + noun/-ing
3. However, + sentence
4. Even though + clause A. Conjunctive adverb starting a new contrasting sentence
B. Preposition followed by a noun phrase or gerund
C. Subordinating conjunction introducing a contrasting clause
D. Emphatic subordinator highlighting sharp unexpected contrast
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Although + clause) → C (Subordinating conjunction introducing a contrasting clause); 2 (Despite + noun/-ing) → B (Preposition followed by a noun phrase or gerund); 3 (However, + sentence) → A (Conjunctive adverb starting a new contrasting sentence); 4 (Even though + clause) → D (Emphatic subordinator highlighting sharp unexpected contrast). To'siqsizlik shakllari: Although/Even though (+ gap), Despite (+ ot/gerund), However (+ yangi gap).
mnemonic: Although + clause / Despite + noun/-ing / However, + sentence / Even though + clause

q:
Match each summary/closing cue with its register and tone:
1. In conclusion
2. Taken together
3. All in all
4. Thus A. Formal essay marker opening the closing paragraph
B. Concise formal deduction closing a logical chain
C. Academic synthesis uniting several prior findings
D. Semi-formal holistic wrap-up of everyday reflections
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (In conclusion) → A (Formal essay marker opening the closing paragraph); 2 (Taken together) → C (Academic synthesis uniting several prior findings); 3 (All in all) → D (Semi-formal holistic wrap-up of everyday reflections); 4 (Thus) → B (Concise formal deduction closing a logical chain). Xulosa belgilari: In conclusion (rasmiy yakun), Taken together (sintez), All in all (yarim rasmiy umumlashma), Thus (ixcham mantiqiy yakun).
mnemonic: In conclusion / Taken together / All in all / Thus

q:
Match each academic signposting phrase with its place in an article:
1. This paper examines...
2. Turning now to...
3. As illustrated in Table 2,
4. Future studies should... A. Mid-article pivot shifting smoothly to a new section
B. Closing section proposing next research directions
C. Body commentary anchoring prose to visual evidence
D. Opening introduction announcing scope and focus
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (This paper examines...) → D (Opening introduction announcing scope and focus); 2 (Turning now to...) → A (Mid-article pivot shifting smoothly to a new section); 3 (As illustrated in Table 2,) → C (Body commentary anchoring prose to visual evidence); 4 (Future studies should...) → B (Closing section proposing next research directions). Ilmiy yo'naltirgichlar (signposting): kirish, bo'lim o'zgarishi, jadvalga havola va kelgusi tadqiqot taklifi.
mnemonic: This paper examines... / Turning now to... / As illustrated in Table 2, / Future studies should...

q:
Match each substitution/ellipsis sentence with the exact type used:
1. She likes green tea; I prefer black.
2. Did they finish early? I hope so.
3. He bought a red bike and I a blue one.
4. They asked us to join, and we did. A. Nominal ellipsis omitting "tea" after "black"
B. Nominal substitution replacing "bike" with "one"
C. Clausal substitution replacing the full clause with "so"
D. Verbal substitution replacing "joined" with "did"
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (She likes green tea; I prefer black.) → A (Nominal ellipsis omitting "tea" after "black"); 2 (Did they finish early? I hope so.) → C (Clausal substitution replacing the full clause with "so"); 3 (He bought a red bike and I a blue one.) → B (Nominal substitution replacing "bike" with "one"); 4 (They asked us to join, and we did.) → D (Verbal substitution replacing "joined" with "did"). O'rinbosarlik va tushirish namunalari: black [tea] (ellipsis), hope so (clausal), blue one (nominal), we did (verbal).
mnemonic: She likes green tea; I prefer black. / Did they finish early? I hope so. / He bought a red bike and I a blue one. / They asked us to join, and we did.

q:
Match each cohesion concept (Halliday & Hasan) with its core domain:
1. Reference
2. Conjunction
3. Lexical cohesion
4. Coherence A. Tracking identity across clauses via pronouns and demonstratives
B. Weaving meaning via synonyms, antonyms, and semantic fields
C. Overall conceptual logic making a text make unified sense
D. Signaling explicit logical ties like cause, contrast, and time
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Reference) → A (Tracking identity across clauses via pronouns and demonstratives); 2 (Conjunction) → D (Signaling explicit logical ties like cause, contrast, and time); 3 (Lexical cohesion) → B (Weaving meaning via synonyms, antonyms, and semantic fields); 4 (Coherence) → C (Overall conceptual logic making a text make unified sense). Halliday & Hasan yaxlitlik nazariyasi: Reference (havola), Conjunction (bog'lovchi), Lexical cohesion (leksik zanjir) va Coherence (umumiy mantiqiy izchillik).

q:
Reorder the five sentences into a coherent academic paragraph on public libraries:
1. A generation ago, visitors entered chiefly to borrow novels or consult heavy encyclopedias.
2. In short, modern libraries now act as essential community hubs for lifelong equity.
3. Neighborhood public libraries have evolved far beyond silent warehouses of printed volumes.
4. Today, however, municipal branches also provide free broadband access and digital-skills mentoring.
5. For instance, job seekers routinely use quiet library booths for remote video interviews.
explanation: Xatboshi tartibi: Mavzu gapi → o'tmish ('A generation ago') → 'Today, however' → 'For instance' → 'In short'.

q:
Arrange the five sentences into a logical problem-solution paragraph on desert irrigation:
1. Open earthen irrigation canals lose nearly half their mountain water to desert evaporation.
2. To counter that loss, engineers are lining channels and testing solar-panel canal canopies.
3. This heavy waste leaves downstream orchards parched during hot August fruit ripening.
4. Consequently, arid valleys can safeguard both scarce rivers and seasonal harvests simultaneously.
5. Shade from these overhead arrays slows evaporation while generating clean power for farm pumps.
explanation: Muammo-yechim tartibi: Muammo → 'This heavy waste' → 'To counter that loss' → 'these overhead arrays' → 'Consequently'.

q:
Sequence the five sentences into a unified paragraph on spaced repetition learning:
1. Each active recall attempt forces the brain to rebuild and strengthen retrieval pathways.
2. By contrast, spaced repetition revisits key concepts across gradually widening intervals.
3. Therefore, twenty focused minutes across five days consistently outperforms one frantic marathon.
4. Although short-term familiarity feels reassuring, neural traces fade swiftly within days.
5. Cramming an entire textbook chapter the night before an exam rarely produces durable mastery.
explanation: Qiyosiy xatboshi: Cramming muammosi → 'Although' → 'By contrast' spaced repetition → 'Each active recall' → 'Therefore'.

q:
Order the five sentences into a coherent paragraph on coastal mangrove restoration:
1. Recognizing this dual value, several coastal cities now fund mangrove replanting over concrete walls.
2. Intact coastal mangrove belts serve as nature's most cost-effective storm barriers.
3. Their tangled underwater roots dissipate fierce cyclone waves long before water hits towns.
4. Ultimately, healthy wetlands protect both vulnerable shorelines and local fishing livelihoods.
5. In addition, calm shaded channels among those roots shelter juvenile fish and crabs.
explanation: Yaxlit xatboshi: Mavzu → 1-mexanizm → 'In addition' 2-mexanizm → 'Recognizing this dual value' → 'Ultimately'.

q:
Arrange the five sentences into a logical paragraph on urban heat islands:
1. Together, cooler materials and urban greenery make summer cities healthier for every resident.
2. Dark asphalt roads absorb solar energy all afternoon and radiate warmth well past midnight.
3. Fortunately, simple architectural changes can soften this uncomfortable urban heat island effect.
4. For example, reflective white roofs and boulevard shade trees cool street surfaces noticeably.
5. Dense concrete downtowns frequently register evening temperatures six degrees higher than nearby farms.
explanation: Xatboshi tartibi: Hodisa → sabab ('Dark asphalt') → 'Fortunately' yechim → 'For example' → 'Together' xulosa.

q:
Sequence the five sentences into a coherent paragraph on handwritten note-taking:
1. They must therefore listen actively, filter central claims, and paraphrase ideas concisely.
2. As a result, longhand note-takers frequently score higher on conceptual exams weeks later.
3. Laptops allow university students to type nearly every spoken lecture word verbatim.
4. Students taking notes by hand, conversely, cannot write fast enough to copy everything.
5. Yet cognitive trials suggest that rapid transcription often bypasses deeper conceptual engagement.
explanation: Mantiqiy zanjir: Laptop tezligi → 'Yet' sayozlik → 'conversely' qo'lda yozish → 'therefore' qayta ishlash → 'As a result'.

q:
Order the five sentences into a unified paragraph on bilingual executive control:
1. Over years, this constant mental juggling exercises neural networks governing focused attention.
2. Thus, sustaining a heritage tongue alongside English offers enduring intellectual advantages.
3. Whenever a bilingual speaker chats in English, the brain quietly suppresses competing Uzbek words.
4. Growing up with two daily languages shapes far more than a child's vocabulary list.
5. Neuroimaging studies confirm that bilingual adults switch smoothly between shifting cognitive rules.
explanation: Xatboshi tartibi: Mavzu → mexanizm → 'this constant mental juggling' → tadqiqot dalili → 'Thus' xulosa.

q:
Arrange the five sentences into a coherent paragraph on circular electronics repair:
1. Millions of laptops and smartphones are discarded prematurely each year despite working processors.
2. To curb this mounting electronic waste, advocates promote modular right-to-repair designs.
3. Standard screws and affordable spare parts allow local shops to extend device lifespans easily.
4. Frequently, a single glued battery or cracked charging port forces owners to replace whole devices.
5. In the end, repairable electronics protect household budgets while reducing rare-metal mining.
explanation: Muammo-yechim zanjiri: E-chiqindi → 'Frequently' sabab → 'To curb this' yechim → amaliy mexanizm → 'In the end'.

q:
Sequence the five sentences into a logical paragraph on peer review in science:
1. Authors must then revise their analyses and address every valid critique satisfactorily.
2. Only after passing that demanding gauntlet does research enter the trusted scholarly record.
3. This rigorous scrutiny frequently uncovers calculation flaws or unsupported conclusions early.
4. Before a journal prints a new clinical study, anonymous experts inspect its methods and statistics.
5. Independent peer review remains the central quality filter of modern scientific publishing.
explanation: Jarayon xatboshisi: Mavzu → 'Before' taqriz → 'This rigorous scrutiny' → 'then revise' → 'Only after passing'.

q:
Order the five sentences into a coherent paragraph on wildlife highway bridges:
1. Attempting to cross busy asphalt exposes deer and motorists alike to dangerous nighttime crashes.
2. Multi-lane expressways slice historic forest habitats into isolated fragments for wild animals.
3. Within months of opening, collisions plunge while isolated animal populations reconnect naturally.
4. Covered with native shrubs and soil, these broad bridges guide herds safely above traffic.
5. Vegetated wildlife overpasses offer a proven engineering solution to this ecological barrier.
explanation: Muammo-yechim tartibi: Yo'l bo'linishi → to'qnashuv xavfi → 'this ecological barrier' yechimi → 'these broad bridges' → natija.

q: Choose the grammatically accurate inverted structure to complete the formal sentence: "Not until the committee reviewed the audited figures _____ the full scale of the deficit."
opts: it recognized
recognized it
did it recognize
it did recognize
explanation: Gap boshida inkor cheklovchi 'Not until + ergash gap' kelganda, bosh gapda qisman inversiya (yordamchi fe'l + ega + asosiy fe'l: 'did it recognize') qo'llanilishi shart.
mnemonic: Not until [clause] + did + S + V1 (negative inversion)

q: Identify the grammatically correct mixed conditional expressing a past unreal condition with a present consequence: "If the architect _____ the seismic fault in 1998, the bridge would be safe for heavy traffic today."
opts: would detect
detected
had detected
has detected
explanation: Aralash shart gapda (Mixed Conditional: o'tgan zamondagi amalga oshmagan shart → hozirgi natija) if-qismda Past Perfect ('had detected'), bosh gapda esa 'would + V1' ('would be') ishlatiladi.
mnemonic: Past unreal (had + V3) → Present result (would + V1)

q: Spot the grammatical error and its precise cause in the sentence: "Neither the principal nor the science teachers was informed about the sudden timetable change."
opts: "about" should be "for" because "inform" strictly governs the preposition "for"
"was" should be "were" to agree with the nearer plural subject "teachers"
"nor" should be "or" because "neither" pairs with "or" in formal English
"informed" should be "informing" because the clause needs an active participle
explanation: 'Neither ... nor ...' bog'lovchisida kesim o'ziga eng yaqin turgan ega bilan shaxs-sonda moslashadi (proximity rule). Yaqin ega 'teachers' ko'plikda bo'lgani uchun 'were' kerak.
mnemonic: Neither A nor B → verb agrees with closer subject B

q: Choose the accurate reporting-passive transformation preserving the exact meaning of: "People currently believe that the manuscript was composed in Samarkand during the fifteenth century."
opts: The manuscript is believed to have been composed in Samarkand.
The manuscript was believed to be composed in Samarkand.
The manuscript was believed to have been composed in Samarkand.
The manuscript is believed to be composed in Samarkand.
explanation: Hozirgi e'tiqod ('is believed') o'tgan zamondagi majhul harakatga ('was composed') tegishli bo'lsa, Perfect Passive Infinitive ('to have been composed') qo'llaniladi.
mnemonic: is believed + past passive → to have been + V3

q: Complete the formal recommendation using the mandative subjunctive: "The ethics board insisted that every applicant _____ an independent declaration before the interview."
opts: submit
submits
to submit
submitted
explanation: 'Insist / recommend / demand + that' dan keyin rasmiy ingliz tilida buyruq-istak mayli (mandative subjunctive) sifatida fe'lning -s siz va to siz asosiy shakli ('submit') ishlatiladi.

q: Select the sentence that uses a non-defining relative clause with completely accurate punctuation and pronoun choice:
opts: My colleague, that work covers bilingualism, won a major grant.
My colleague, whose work covers bilingualism, won a grant.
My colleague, who's work covers bilingualism, won a national grant.
My colleague whose work covers bilingualism, won a national grant.
explanation: Aniqlovchi emas (non-defining) ergash gap ikki tomondan vergul bilan ajratiladi, egalik uchun 'whose' ishlatiladi ('who's' = 'who is', 'that' esa verguldan keyin qo'llanmaydi).
mnemonic: Non-defining: commas both sides + whose (not who's/that)

q: Choose the option that accurately distinguishes the meaning of "stopped to check" versus "stopped checking": "Halfway up the trail, the hikers stopped _____ their compass before entering the mist."
opts: checking (paused walking in order to consult the compass)
checking (permanently gave up consulting their compass)
to check (paused walking in order to consult the compass)
to check (permanently gave up consulting their compass)
explanation: 'Stop + to-infinitive' maqsad uchun to'xtashni ('kompasni tekshirish uchun to'xtadi'), 'stop + -ing' esa harakatni butunlay to'xtatishni bildiradi.
mnemonic: stop + to V = pause in order to; stop + V-ing = quit doing

q: Complete the sentence with the correct participle clause: "_____ through three rounds of blind peer review, the paper was finally accepted for the spring issue."
opts: Passing
Having passed
To passing
Passed
explanation: Maqola qabul qilinishidan oldin uch bosqichli taqrizdan o'tib bo'lganini (oldingi tugallangan faol harakat) ifodalash uchun Perfect Participle ('Having passed') qo'llaniladi.
mnemonic: Completed prior action → Having + V3 (Perfect Participle)

q:
Match each advanced grammatical structure with its authentic sentence example:
1. Cleft sentence
2. Negative inversion
3. Subjunctive mood
4. Causative passive A. We had the laboratory microscopes calibrated last Tuesday.
B. The dean requested that the report be revised immediately.
C. It was the sudden frost that ruined the early apricot blossom.
D. Rarely have meteorologists recorded such dry winter winds.
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Cleft sentence) → C (It was the sudden frost that ruined the early apricot blossom.); 2 (Negative inversion) → D (Rarely have meteorologists recorded such dry winter winds.); 3 (Subjunctive mood) → B (The dean requested that the report be revised immediately.); 4 (Causative passive) → A (We had the laboratory microscopes calibrated last Tuesday.). Cleft sentence ('It was... that...') urg'u berish; Negative inversion ('Rarely have...'); Subjunctive ('be revised'); Causative ('had ... calibrated' — birovga qildirish).
mnemonic: Cleft-It was, Inversion-Rarely have, Subjunctive-be, Causative-have sth done

q:
Arrange the English adjective categories in standard pre-nominal order (OSASCOMP) before a noun:
1. Material adjective (e.g. ceramic, wooden)
2. Age adjective (e.g. antique, medieval)
3. Opinion adjective (e.g. elegant, remarkable)
4. Size adjective (e.g. enormous, compact)
5. Origin adjective (e.g. Uzbek, Venetian)
explanation: Ingliz tilida sifatlar otdan oldin qat'iy tartibda keladi: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose (masalan: an elegant large antique Uzbek ceramic vase).
mnemonic: OSASCOMP: Opinion → Size → Age → Origin → Material

q: Choose the precise verb that completes the natural academic collocation: "Before launching the nationwide literacy survey, the ministry will _____ a pilot study in twelve schools."
opts: produce
make
conduct
commit
explanation: 'Study / survey / experiment / research' otlari bilan tabiiy akademik kollokatsiya sifatida 'conduct' (o'tkazmoq) fe'li qo'llaniladi; 'make/commit a study' leksik jihatdan noto'g'ri.
mnemonic: conduct a pilot study / survey / research

q: Choose the exact near-synonym that fits the grammar and meaning of the sentence: "During the panel discussion, Dr. Karimova _____ the delegates that the revised syllabus would take effect in September."
opts: said
told
talked
spoke
explanation: To'g'ridan-to'g'ri shaxs to'ldiruvchisi ('the delegates') + 'that'-gap kelganda odatda 'tell' ('told the delegates that...') grammatik va leksik jihatdan to'g'ri; 'say/speak/talk' dan keyin 'to' predlogi talab qilinadi.
mnemonic: tell + someone + that (no 'to'); say + to someone

q: Select the derived word that accurately completes the sentence through word formation: "The witness gave such a _____ account of the evening that investigators could not verify the timeline."
opts: contradiction
contradict
contradictorily
contradictory
explanation: 'Account' (hisobot/guvohlik) otini aniqlash uchun 'contradict' fe'lidan yasalgan sifat shakli — 'contradictory' (ziddiyatli) talab etiladi.

q: Choose the closest contextual synonym for "mitigate" in the sentence: "Expanding urban green corridors can significantly mitigate the health risks of summer heatwaves."
opts: instigate
alleviate
aggravate
fabricate
explanation: 'Mitigate' xavf yoki zararning og'irligini yumshatish, kamaytirish degani; uning kontekstual sinonimi 'alleviate' (yengillashtirmoq). 'Aggravate' esa aksincha kuchaytirish (antonim).

q: Identify the lexical collocation error in the formal sentence: "The new safety protocol has brought a strong improvement in laboratory compliance across regional colleges."
opts: "regional colleges" is an overly informal phrase for institutional prose
"strong improvement" should be "marked improvement" in standard usage
"laboratory compliance" must become "laboratory obedience" in prose
"safety protocol" is wrong and should be replaced with "safe protocol"
explanation: Ingliz tilida 'improvement' oti 'strong' bilan emas, balki 'marked / significant / substantial / dramatic improvement' kollokatsiyalari bilan qo'llaniladi.

q: Select the phrasal verb that accurately matches the meaning "to reluctantly accept or tolerate an unpleasant situation": "Residents near the construction site had to _____ constant drilling for six months."
opts: come up with
catch up with
do away with
put up with
explanation: 'Put up with' — noqulay vaziyatga chidamoq, toqat qilmoq; 'come up with' — g'oya o'ylab topmoq; 'catch up with' — yetib olmoq; 'do away with' — bekor qilmoq.

q: Choose the option that clashes with the formal academic register of the sentence: "The longitudinal study revealed that bilingual toddlers _____ cognitive flexibility slightly earlier than monolingual peers."
opts: develop (neutral academic verb for acquiring skills)
demonstrate (appropriate verb for observable evidence)
pick up on kinda (too colloquial for academic prose)
exhibit (standard formal verb in scientific reporting)
explanation: Akademik maqolada 'exhibit / develop / demonstrate' rasmiy fe'llari mos keladi; 'pick up on kinda' esa o'ta og'zaki-norasmiy (colloquial) bo'lib, registrga zid.
mnemonic: Academic register rejects colloquial 'kinda / pick up on'

q:
Match each Gricean conversational maxim with its core communicative rule:
1. Maxim of Quantity
2. Maxim of Quality
3. Maxim of Relation
4. Maxim of Manner A. Be truthful and avoid claims lacking adequate evidence
B. Give as much information as needed, neither too much nor too little
C. Express yourself clearly, briefly, and without unnecessary ambiguity
D. Ensure your contribution is relevant to the current exchange
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Maxim of Quantity) → B (Give as much information as needed, neither too much nor too little); 2 (Maxim of Quality) → A (Be truthful and avoid claims lacking adequate evidence); 3 (Maxim of Relation) → D (Ensure your contribution is relevant to the current exchange); 4 (Maxim of Manner) → C (Express yourself clearly, briefly, and without unnecessary ambiguity). Grice 4 tamoyili: Quantity (yetarli miqdor), Quality (rostgo'ylik), Relation (mavzuga daxldorlik), Manner (aniq va tushunarli bayon).

q:

D. If + Present Simple, will + V1 (real future)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Zero conditional) → C (If + Present Simple, Present Simple (general truth)); 2 (First conditional) → D (If + Present Simple, will + V1 (real future)); 3 (Second conditional) → A (If + Past Simple, would + V1 (unreal present/future)); 4 (Third conditional) → B (If + Past Perfect, would have + V3 (unreal past)). Shart gaplar 4 asosiy turi: Zero (umumiy fakt), First (real kelajak), Second (noreal hozir), Third (noreal o'tmish).
mnemonic: Zero conditional / First conditional / Second conditional / Third conditional

explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Should you need...) → B (Formal replacement for "If you happen to need..."); 2 (Were she to apply...) → A (Formal replacement for "If she applied..."); 3 (Had they known...) → D (Formal replacement for "If they had known..."); 4 (Were it not for...) → C (Formal replacement for "If it weren't for..."). Inversiyali shart gaplar: Should (1-tur), Were+to (2-tur), Had+V3 (3-tur), Were it not for (mavjud omilsiz).

q:

B. Near-certain negative impossibility in the past
C. Criticism or regret over an unperformed past duty
D. Near-certain positive deduction about a past event
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (must have left) → D (Near-certain positive deduction about a past event); 2 (can't have broken) → B (Near-certain negative impossibility in the past); 3 (needn't have bought) → A (Action was performed though it proved unnecessary); 4 (should have checked) → C (Criticism or regret over an unperformed past duty). O'tgan zamon modallari: must have (aniq bo'lgan), can't have (bo'lishi mumkin emas), needn't have (bekor qilingan), should have (qilish kerak edi).

q:

B. ... than (immediate sequence of two past actions)
C. ... when (barely finished before next action)
D. ... but also (adding a second emphatic point)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (No sooner ...) → B (... than (immediate sequence of two past actions)); 2 (Hardly / Scarcely ...) → C (... when (barely finished before next action)); 3 (Not only ...) → D (... but also (adding a second emphatic point)); 4 (Not until + clause ...) → A (... did + S + V1 (inversion occurs in main clause)). Inversiya juftliklari: No sooner... than, Hardly/Scarcely... when, Not only... but also, Not until [ergash] + [bosh gap inversiyasi].

q:

B. Walking through the park, they spotted rare cranes.
C. Having finished the rubric, she emailed the team.
D. Built in 1420, the observatory stood atop a hill.
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Present participle) → B (Walking through the park, they spotted rare cranes.); 2 (Past participle (passive)) → D (Built in 1420, the observatory stood atop a hill.); 3 (Perfect participle) → C (Having finished the rubric, she emailed the team.); 4 (Negative participle) → A (Not knowing the shortcut, we took the main road.). Sifatdoshli o'ramlar: Present (faol bir paytda), Past (majhul), Perfect (oldingi tugallangan), Negative (Not + V-ing).

q:

2. Non-defining clause
3. Sentential ", which"
4. Preposition + whom A. Refers back to the entire preceding main clause
B. Formal human object pattern after a preposition
C. Extra non-essential info set off by commas (no "that")
D. Essential identifier written without enclosing commas
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Defining clause) → D (Essential identifier written without enclosing commas); 2 (Non-defining clause) → C (Extra non-essential info set off by commas (no "that")); 3 (Sentential ", which") → A (Refers back to the entire preceding main clause); 4 (Preposition + whom) → B (Formal human object pattern after a preposition). Nisbiy ergash gaplar: Defining (vergulsiz), Non-defining (vergulli, that yo'q), Sentential (, which), Formal (to/with whom).
mnemonic: Defining clause / Non-defining clause / Sentential ", which" / Preposition + whom

q:

q:

B. Formal preposition preceding a noun phrase

explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Although / Even though) → C (Followed directly by a full subject-verb clause); 2 (Despite / In spite of) → D (Followed by a noun phrase, pronoun, or gerund); 3 (Adj + though + S + be) → A (Fronted adjective for formal emphatic concession); 4 (Notwithstanding) → B (Formal preposition preceding a noun phrase). To'siqsizlik tuzilmalari: Although (+ gap), Despite (+ ot/V-ing), Exhausted though they were (inversiyali urg'u), Notwithstanding (+ ot).

q:

C. Prior plan or visible present evidence
D. Action in progress at a specific future moment
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Future Simple (will V1)) → A (Spontaneous decision or general prediction); 2 (Be going to + V1) → C (Prior plan or visible present evidence); 3 (Future Continuous) → D (Action in progress at a specific future moment); 4 (Future Perfect) → B (Action completed before a stated future deadline). Kelasi zamonlar: will (tezkor qaror), going to (reja/belgi), Future Continuous (jarayon), Future Perfect (muddatgacha tugallanish).
mnemonic: Future Simple (will V1) / Be going to + V1 / Future Continuous / Future Perfect

q:
Match each causative construction with its grammatical structure:
1. have + sth + V3
2. get + sth + V3
3. have + sb + bare V1
4. get + sb + to V1 A. Persuading or convincing a person to act
B. Instructing or authorizing a person to act
C. Informal/effortful arrangement of a service done
D. Formal/neutral arrangement of a service done
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (have + sth + V3) → D (Formal/neutral arrangement of a service done); 2 (get + sth + V3) → C (Informal/effortful arrangement of a service done); 3 (have + sb + bare V1) → B (Instructing or authorizing a person to act); 4 (get + sb + to V1) → A (Persuading or convincing a person to act). Kauzativ tuzilmalar: have/get sth done (xizmat qildirish), have sb do (topshirish), get sb to do (ko'ndirish).
mnemonic: have + sth + V3 / get + sth + V3 / have + sb + bare V1 / get + sb + to V1

q:
Match each uncountable academic noun with its correct countable unit:
1. advice
2. equipment
3. research
4. furniture A. an item of equipment (never "equipments")
B. a piece of advice (never "an advice")
C. a piece of furniture (never "furnitures")
D. a body/study of research (never "researches")
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (advice) → B (a piece of advice (never "an advice")); 2 (equipment) → A (an item of equipment (never "equipments")); 3 (research) → D (a body/study of research (never "researches")); 4 (furniture) → C (a piece of furniture (never "furnitures")). Sanalmaydigan akademik otlar: advice, equipment, research, furniture — birlikda keladi va -s olmaydi.

q:
Match each comparative structure with its accurate English model:
1. Double comparative
2. Proportional comparative
3. Multiplier comparison
4. Latinate comparative A. The more we read, the richer our style grows
B. Superior to / prior to (takes "to", never "than")
C. Faster and faster (gradual ongoing increase)
D. Twice as efficient as older models (not "than")
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Double comparative) → C (Faster and faster (gradual ongoing increase)); 2 (Proportional comparative) → A (The more we read, the richer our style grows); 3 (Multiplier comparison) → D (Twice as efficient as older models (not "than")); 4 (Latinate comparative) → B (Superior to / prior to (takes "to", never "than")). Qiyoslash qoliplari: faster and faster, The more... the more, twice as... as, superior/prior to.
mnemonic: Double comparative / Proportional comparative / Multiplier comparison / Latinate comparative

q:
Match each verb-plus-preposition pattern with the preposition it governs:
1. insist
2. succeed
3. object
4. abstain A. insist + on + V-ing
B. object + to + V-ing
C. succeed + in + V-ing
D. abstain + from + V-ing
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (insist) → A (insist + on + V-ing); 2 (succeed) → C (succeed + in + V-ing); 3 (object) → B (object + to + V-ing); 4 (abstain) → D (abstain + from + V-ing). Fe'l + predlog + gerund: insist on, succeed in, object to, abstain from.

q:
Match each aspect of past time with its authentic narrative role:
1. Past Simple
2. Past Continuous
3. Past Perfect Simple
4. Past Perfect Continuous A. Earlier event finished before another past point
B. Duration of an earlier activity up to a past point
C. Interrupted ongoing scene at a past instant
D. Completed chronological event in a past chain
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Past Simple) → D (Completed chronological event in a past chain); 2 (Past Continuous) → C (Interrupted ongoing scene at a past instant); 3 (Past Perfect Simple) → A (Earlier event finished before another past point); 4 (Past Perfect Continuous) → B (Duration of an earlier activity up to a past point). O'tgan zamon turlari: Simple (tugallangan), Continuous (davomiy fon), Perfect (avvalgi), Perfect Continuous (avvalgi davomiylik).
mnemonic: Past Simple / Past Continuous / Past Perfect Simple / Past Perfect Continuous

q:
Match each purpose clause connector with its exact grammatical frame:
1. in order to
2. so that
3. for + V-ing
4. lest A. Describes the general function of a tool/object
B. Formal negative purpose ("for fear that") + subjunctive
C. Followed by subject + modal (can/could/may)
D. Followed by bare infinitive for intentional goal
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (in order to) → D (Followed by bare infinitive for intentional goal); 2 (so that) → C (Followed by subject + modal (can/could/may)); 3 (for + V-ing) → A (Describes the general function of a tool/object); 4 (lest) → B (Formal negative purpose ("for fear that") + subjunctive). Maqsad bog'lovchilari: in order to (+ V1), so that (+ gap), for (+ V-ing, asbob vazifasi), lest (+ subjunctive).
mnemonic: in order to / so that / for + V-ing / lest

q:
Match each determiner with the noun class it pairs with:
1. every
2. each
3. either
4. both A. Emphasizes individual items separately (two or more)
B. Refers to all members of a group of three or more
C. Refers to one or the other of exactly two items
D. Refers jointly to two items together (takes plural)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (every) → B (Refers to all members of a group of three or more); 2 (each) → A (Emphasizes individual items separately (two or more)); 3 (either) → C (Refers to one or the other of exactly two items); 4 (both) → D (Refers jointly to two items together (takes plural)). Aniqlovchilar: every (3+ hammasi), each (alohida har biri), either (ikkidan biri), both (ikkalasi).

q:
Match each adverb position with its standard English sentence slot:
1. Mid-position frequency
2. End-position manner
3. Front-position viewpoint
4. Post-auxiliary focus A. Follows first auxiliary (e.g. has already completed)
B. After verb/object (e.g. calibrated the gauge carefully)
C. Before main verb, after "be" (e.g. rarely, always)
D. Opens sentence with comma (e.g. Economically, ...)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Mid-position frequency) → C (Before main verb, after "be" (e.g. rarely, always)); 2 (End-position manner) → B (After verb/object (e.g. calibrated the gauge carefully)); 3 (Front-position viewpoint) → D (Opens sentence with comma (e.g. Economically, ...)); 4 (Post-auxiliary focus) → A (Follows first auxiliary (e.g. has already completed)). Ravish o'rni: frequency (asosiy fe'ldan oldin), manner (oxirida), viewpoint (gap boshida), post-auxiliary (yordamchi fe'ldan keyin).
mnemonic: Mid-position frequency / End-position manner / Front-position viewpoint / Post-auxiliary focus

q:
Match each tag-question rule with its correct example:
1. Negative statement
2. Imperative invitation
3. Sentence with "seldom"
4. Statement with "I am" A. She seldom misses class, does she? (positive tag)
B. I'm on the shortlist, aren't I?
C. Pass me the rubric, will you?
D. They haven't finished, have they? (positive tag)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Negative statement) → D (They haven't finished, have they? (positive tag)); 2 (Imperative invitation) → C (Pass me the rubric, will you?); 3 (Sentence with "seldom") → A (She seldom misses class, does she? (positive tag)); 4 (Statement with "I am") → B (I'm on the shortlist, aren't I?). Qisqa tasdiq savollari (Question tags): inkor→tasdiq, buyruq→will you, seldom→does she, I am→aren't I.
mnemonic: Negative statement / Imperative invitation / Sentence with "seldom" / Statement with "I am"

q:
Match each noun-clause starter with its syntactic function:
1. Whether ... or not
2. That + clause (subject)
3. Whoever + verb
4. How + adj + S + V A. Introduces binary indirect choice without "if" at start
B. Means "any person who" as clause subject
C. Embeds degree inside an indirect exclamation/question
D. Acts formally as subject ("That he passed pleased us")
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Whether ... or not) → A (Introduces binary indirect choice without "if" at start); 2 (That + clause (subject)) → D (Acts formally as subject ("That he passed pleased us")); 3 (Whoever + verb) → B (Means "any person who" as clause subject); 4 (How + adj + S + V) → C (Embeds degree inside an indirect exclamation/question). Ot ergash gaplari: Whether (boshida if ishlatilmaydi), That-subject, Whoever, How+adj.
mnemonic: Whether ... or not / That + clause (subject) / Whoever + verb / How + adj + S + V

q:
Match each tense shift in formal reported speech with its rule:
1. Present Simple → Past Simple
2. Past Simple → Past Perfect
3. will → would
4. Universal scientific truth A. Often remains Present Simple as timeless fact
B. Standard backshift when reporting verb is past
C. Marks completed action prior to past reporting time
D. Backshifts future prediction inside past reporting
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Present Simple → Past Simple) → B (Standard backshift when reporting verb is past); 2 (Past Simple → Past Perfect) → C (Marks completed action prior to past reporting time); 3 (will → would) → D (Backshifts future prediction inside past reporting); 4 (Universal scientific truth) → A (Often remains Present Simple as timeless fact). O'zlashtirma gapda zamon moslashuvi: Present→Past, Past→Past Perfect, will→would, umumiy ilmiy haqiqat o'zgarmasligi mumkin.
mnemonic: Present Simple → Past Simple / Past Simple → Past Perfect / will → would / Universal scientific truth

q:
Match each punctuation error type with its grammatical diagnosis:
1. Comma splice
2. Dangling participle
3. Split restrictive relative
4. Misplaced apostrophe A. Writing "who's" (who is) instead of possessive "whose"
B. Opening participle doesn't match the main clause subject
C. Putting commas around an essential defining clause
D. Joining two full clauses with only a comma (needs ;)
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (Comma splice) → D (Joining two full clauses with only a comma (needs ;)); 2 (Dangling participle) → B (Opening participle doesn't match the main clause subject); 3 (Split restrictive relative) → C (Putting commas around an essential defining clause); 4 (Misplaced apostrophe) → A (Writing "who's" (who is) instead of possessive "whose"). Sintaktik va punktuatsion xatolar: comma splice, dangling participle, defining gapga vergul qo'yish va who's/whose chalkashligi.
mnemonic: Comma splice / Dangling participle / Split restrictive relative / Misplaced apostrophe

q:
Match each complex preposition with its accurate grammatical meaning:
1. owing to
2. regardless of
3. by means of
4. in light of A. Expresses indifference to an obstacle ("despite")
B. Expresses method or instrument used to achieve a goal
C. Expresses consideration of newly revealed evidence
D. Expresses cause ("because of") before a noun phrase
explanation: To'g'ri moslik: 1 (owing to) → D (Expresses cause ("because of") before a noun phrase); 2 (regardless of) → A (Expresses indifference to an obstacle ("despite")); 3 (by means of) → B (Expresses method or instrument used to achieve a goal); 4 (in light of) → C (Expresses consideration of newly revealed evidence). Murakkab predloglar: owing to (sababli), regardless of (qat'i nazar), by means of (orqali), in light of (nuqtayi nazaridan).
mnemonic: owing to / regardless of / by means of / in light of

q:
Order these five pre-nominal adjective slots according to standard English adjective order:
1. Material (e.g. ceramic, cedar)
2. Determiner (e.g. these, several)
3. Opinion (e.g. exquisite, rare)
4. Color (e.g. turquoise, crimson)
5. Shape (e.g. octagonal, slender)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Determiner (e.g. these, several) → 2) Opinion (e.g. exquisite, rare) → 3) Shape (e.g. octagonal, slender) → 4) Color (e.g. turquoise, crimson) → 5) Material (e.g. ceramic, cedar). Sifatlar tartibi (OSASCOMP): Determiner → Opinion → Shape → Color → Material.

q:
Arrange the components of a negative-inversion sentence from first element to last:
1. Grammatical subject (e.g. the committee)
2. Direct object and modifiers (e.g. the missing figure)
3. Inverted auxiliary verb (e.g. did)
4. Base form of main verb (e.g. recognize)
5. Negative/restrictive adverbial opener (e.g. Not until dusk)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Negative/restrictive adverbial opener (e.g. Not until dusk) → 2) Inverted auxiliary verb (e.g. did) → 3) Grammatical subject (e.g. the committee) → 4) Base form of main verb (e.g. recognize) → 5) Direct object and modifiers (e.g. the missing figure). Inversiya sintaktik tartibi: Inkor ochuvchi → yordamchi fe'l → ega → asosiy fe'l → to'ldiruvchi.

q:
Order the canonical sequence of English auxiliaries before a main verb (longest verb phrase):
1. Perfect auxiliary (have)
2. Passive auxiliary (being)
3. Main verb past participle (reviewed)
4. Modal auxiliary (e.g. might)
5. Progressive auxiliary (been)
explanation: Murakkab fe'l zanjiri tartibi: Modal → Perfect (have) → Progressive (been) → Passive (being) → V3 (might have been being reviewed).

q:
Arrange the standard end-position order of English adverbials after an intransitive verb:
1. Time adverbial (e.g. during the 1990s)
2. Place adverbial (e.g. to Bukhara)
3. Frequency adverbial (e.g. twice a year)
4. Manner adverbial (e.g. calmly / by rail)
5. Verb of movement (e.g. traveled)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Verb of movement (e.g. traveled) → 2) Manner adverbial (e.g. calmly / by rail) → 3) Place adverbial (e.g. to Bukhara) → 4) Frequency adverbial (e.g. twice a year) → 5) Time adverbial (e.g. during the 1990s). Hollar tartibi (MPT): Harakat fe'li → Ravish (Manner) → O'rin (Place) → Takror → Payt (Time).

q:
Order the steps to transform an active sentence into a reporting passive correctly:
1. Convert the reporting verb into passive voice ("is believed")
2. Attach the matching infinitive ("to have left" for prior past action)
3. Promote the subordinate subject ("He") to main-clause subject position
4. Identify the active reporting verb and subordinate clause ("People believe he left")
5. Check whether the subordinate event happened earlier than the belief
explanation: Reporting passive yasash: ega ko'chirish → passiv fe'l → zamon farqini tekshirish → mos infinitiv (to have V3).

q:
Sequence the grammatical steps to convert a direct quote into formal reported speech:
1. Adjust first- and second-person pronouns to the reporter's perspective
2. Shift deictic time and place words ("tomorrow" → "the next day")
3. Backshift finite verbs one tense backward when applicable
4. Remove quotation marks and verify indirect question word order
5. Identify the tense of the reporting verb (e.g. said / explained)
explanation: O'zlashtirma gapga o'tkazish: reporting verb → olmoshlar → zamon orqaga surilishi → payt/o'rin so'zlari → qo'shtirnoqni olish.

q:
Order these five English verb tenses chronologically from earliest past to latest future:
1. Future Perfect (will have sealed by Friday)
2. Past Simple (sealed yesterday)
3. Past Perfect (had already sealed)
4. Present Simple (seals routinely)
5. Future Continuous (will be sealing tomorrow)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Past Perfect (had already sealed) → 2) Past Simple (sealed yesterday) → 3) Present Simple (seals routinely) → 4) Future Continuous (will be sealing tomorrow) → 5) Future Perfect (will have sealed by Friday). Zamon chizig'i: Past Perfect → Past Simple → Present Simple → Future Continuous → Future Perfect.

q:
Arrange the syntactic components of an It-cleft sentence in exact order:
1. Relative linker ("that" or "who")
2. Highlighted focused constituent (e.g. the sudden frost)
3. Introductory dummy pronoun "It"
4. Remaining background clause ("ruined the buds")
5. Tense-matched form of "be" (is / was)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Introductory dummy pronoun "It" → 2) Tense-matched form of "be" (is / was) → 3) Highlighted focused constituent (e.g. the sudden frost) → 4) Relative linker ("that" or "who") → 5) Remaining background clause ("ruined the buds"). It-cleft tuzilmasi: It + is/was + urg'uli bo'lak + that/who + qolgan gap.

q:
Order the five grammatical layers of an English noun phrase from left to right:
1. Pre-modifying adjective (e.g. antique)
2. Post-determiner quantifier (e.g. three / several)
3. Central determiner (e.g. the / those)
4. Head noun (e.g. manuscripts)
5. Pre-determiner (e.g. all / half)
explanation: Otli birikma tartibi: Pre-determiner (all) → Determiner (the) → Quantifier (three) → Adjective (antique) → Head noun (manuscripts).

q:
Sequence the steps to diagnose and fix a dangling participle clause:
1. Spot the opening participle phrase (e.g. "Walking into the hall,...")
2. Check the very first subject appearing right after the comma
3. Identify the implied human agent performing that opening action
4. Rewrite the main clause so the true actor stands directly after the comma
5. Confirm whether the main-clause subject matches the implied agent
explanation: Osilib qolgan sifatdoshni (dangling participle) tuzatish bosqichlari: o'ram → haqiqiy bajaruvchi → verguldan keyingi ega → moslashtirish.

q:
Order these modals of present deduction from 0% impossibility up to near-100% certainty:
1. It must be right (near-certain logical deduction)
2. It could be right (open possibility)
3. It might not be right (possible negation)
4. It can't be right (logical impossibility)
5. It ought to be right (strong expectation)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) It can't be right (logical impossibility) → 2) It might not be right (possible negation) → 3) It could be right (open possibility) → 4) It ought to be right (strong expectation) → 5) It must be right (near-certain logical deduction). Mantiqiy xulosa shkalasi: can't (0%) → might not → could → ought to → must (~99%).

q:
Arrange the steps for forming an inverted third conditional without "if":
1. Move the auxiliary "Had" to the very front before the subject
2. Keep "not" after the subject if the clause is negative ("Had they not...")
3. Delete the subordinating conjunction "If" completely
4. Start with the full third conditional ("If they had checked the gauge...")
5. Preserve the main clause ("they would have spotted the leak") unchanged
explanation: 3-tur inversiya: If ni olib tashlash → Had ni oldinga chiqarish → not ni egadan keyin qoldirish → bosh gapni saqlash.

q:
Sequence the check steps for English subject-verb agreement in complex sentences:
1. Locate the finite main verb needing agreement
2. Determine whether that head is singular, plural, or proximity-governed
3. Identify the true grammatical head noun or pronoun of the subject
4. Select the verb form matching the head in person and number
5. Strip away intervening prepositional phrases ("of...", "along with...")
explanation: Ega-kesim tekshiruvi: fe'lni topish → oraliq iboralarni chetlatish → bosh egaga qarash → birlik/ko'plik → mos kesim.

q:
Order the parts of a formal mandative-subjunctive sentence from opener to ending:
1. Trigger expression of urgency or demand (e.g. "The board insisted")
2. Subordinating complementizer ("that")
3. Required object or complement (e.g. "a signed declaration")
4. Uninflected bare infinitive verb (e.g. "submit" / "be")
5. Target subject of the recommendation (e.g. "every applicant")
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Trigger expression of urgency or demand (e.g. "The board insisted") → 2) Subordinating complementizer ("that") → 3) Target subject of the recommendation (e.g. "every applicant") → 4) Uninflected bare infinitive verb (e.g. "submit" / "be") → 5) Required object or complement (e.g. "a signed declaration"). Mandative subjunctive tuzilmasi: Trigger + that + ega + bare infinitive + to'ldiruvchi.

q:
Arrange the five steps to combine two simple sentences into a non-defining relative clause:
1. Insert the relative clause directly beside the noun it describes
2. Choose the correct non-defining relative pronoun ("who", "which", or "whose" — never "that")
3. Enclose the embedded clause with commas on BOTH sides
4. Confirm the remaining outer main sentence still reads cleanly without it
5. Verify that the second sentence gives extra, non-essential background info
explanation: Non-defining ergash gap yasash: qo'shimcha ma'no → who/which/whose (that emas) → ot yoniga qo'yish → ikki vergul → asosiy gap tekshiruvi.

q:
Order these five levels of English syntactic hierarchy from smallest unit to largest:
1. Clause (e.g. although the sensor worked)
2. Phrase (e.g. the newly calibrated sensor)
3. Morpheme (e.g. un-, -ed)
4. Word (e.g. calibrated)
5. Complex sentence (main clause + subordinate clause)
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Morpheme (e.g. un-, -ed) → 2) Word (e.g. calibrated) → 3) Phrase (e.g. the newly calibrated sensor) → 4) Clause (e.g. although the sensor worked) → 5) Complex sentence (main clause + subordinate clause). Sintaktik iyerarxiya: Morpheme → Word → Phrase → Clause → Complex sentence.

q:
Sequence the diagnostic steps for choosing between "needn't have V3" and "didn't need to V1":
1. If known beforehand and skipped completely, choose "didn't need to + V1"
2. Verify the surrounding context cues ("after all" vs "so we stayed home")
3. If performed needlessly in hindsight, choose "needn't have + V3"
4. Confirm that an action in the past turned out to be unnecessary
5. Ask whether the subject actually went ahead and performed the action
explanation: needn't have vs didn't need to tanlash algoritmi: keraksizligini bilish → bajarilganmi? → Ha: needn't have V3; Yo'q: didn't need to V1.

q:
Order the components of a causative passive sentence ("We had the piano tuned"):
1. Optional agent or time phrase ("by a master technician before the gala")
2. Recipient object receiving the service ("the grand piano")
3. Agent arranging the service ("We")
4. Past participle of the performed action ("tuned")
5. Causative verb matched to tense ("had" / "got")
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Agent arranging the service ("We") → 2) Causative verb matched to tense ("had" / "got") → 3) Recipient object receiving the service ("the grand piano") → 4) Past participle of the performed action ("tuned") → 5) Optional agent or time phrase ("by a master technician before the gala"). Kauzativ tuzilma: Buyurtmachi → have/get → obyekt → V3 → qo'shimcha hol.

q:
Arrange the steps to verify correct "neither ... nor" verb agreement in editing:
1. Match the finite verb strictly to Element B under the proximity rule
2. Check whether Element B is singular or plural
3. Locate Element B standing closest to the main verb
4. Check grammatical parallelism between Element A and Element B
5. Verify both correlative words appear accurately ("neither" paired with "nor")
explanation: To'g'ri xronologik/mantiqiy ketma-ketlik: 1) Verify both correlative words appear accurately ("neither" paired with "nor") → 2) Check grammatical parallelism between Element A and Element B → 3) Locate Element B standing closest to the main verb → 4) Check whether Element B is singular or plural → 5) Match the finite verb strictly to Element B under the proximity rule. Neither...nor tekshiruvi: juftlik → parallelizm → yaqin ega B → soni → kesimni B ga moslash.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "Unregulated plastic dumping can _____ a grave threat to coastal fish nurseries."
opts: pose
create up
build
do
explanation: Akademik va tabiiy ingliz tili kollokatsiyasiga ko'ra aynan 'pose a threat' birikmasi qo'llaniladi; qolgan fe'llar bu ot bilan tabiiy birikma hosil qilmaydi.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "Consistent mentoring helps _____ mutual trust between novice and veteran educators."
opts: foster
cook
push
plant up
explanation: Akademik va tabiiy ingliz tili kollokatsiyasiga ko'ra aynan 'foster trust' birikmasi qo'llaniladi; qolgan fe'llar bu ot bilan tabiiy birikma hosil qilmaydi.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "Careful peer review _____ reliable findings before clinical guidelines change."
opts: yields
makes out
grows
earns up
explanation: Akademik va tabiiy ingliz tili kollokatsiyasiga ko'ra aynan 'yields findings' birikmasi qo'llaniladi; qolgan fe'llar bu ot bilan tabiiy birikma hosil qilmaydi.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "Library Wi-Fi loans help _____ the digital divide for low-income secondary pupils."
opts: tie
bridge
mend
glue
explanation: Akademik va tabiiy ingliz tili kollokatsiyasiga ko'ra aynan 'bridge the divide' birikmasi qo'llaniladi; qolgan fe'llar bu ot bilan tabiiy birikma hosil qilmaydi.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "Urban heat waves _____ immense pressure on older municipal power transformers."
opts: throw
push on
exert
press up
explanation: Akademik va tabiiy ingliz tili kollokatsiyasiga ko'ra aynan 'exert pressure' birikmasi qo'llaniladi; qolgan fe'llar bu ot bilan tabiiy birikma hosil qilmaydi.

q: Choose the natural English collocation to complete the sentence: "The treaty aims to _____ strict limits on untreated industrial river discharge."
opts: place down
force
